before.zh: 1783年3月，纽约州纽堡，大陆军总部。军队向国会递了一份请愿，列了五项：发现饷、结算欠饷并给担保、把终身半薪折算成一笔等值补偿、结算口粮亏欠、结算被服亏欠。国会此前的答复被军中视为"远不能令人满意"，只是和平在即，部队暂时安静。
before.en: In March 1783, at the Continental Army's headquarters in Newburgh, New York, the army sent a petition to Congress listing five items: present pay, a settlement of arrears of pay with security for what was due, a lump-sum equivalent in place of the half pay promised for life, a settlement of the deficiencies of rations, and a settlement of the deficiencies of clothing. Congress's earlier reply was seen in the army as "far from being satisfactory"; only the certainty that peace was near kept the troops quiet for the moment.

before.zh: 就在这时，营中流传起匿名文字，用"匿名召集"的方式把军官们叫到一起，口气里暗示：谁主张再忍一忍，谁就在出卖大家。华盛顿随即在3月11日下令军官于15日集会，又引出了第二封匿名信。他面对的难处很具体：下属的不满有事实根据，而传达不满的方式正在制造新的伤害。
before.en: Just then, anonymous writings began circulating in camp, using "an anonymous summons" to gather the officers together, with a tone that hinted anyone who urged holding on a little longer was selling everyone out. Washington responded with an order of 11 March directing the officers to assemble on the 15th, which in turn produced a second anonymous address. The difficulty he faced was concrete: his subordinates' complaints were well founded, and the way those complaints were voiced was creating new harm.

after.zh: 前一年12月，大陆军派代表去国会递交请愿。国会委员会后来把请愿归纳为五项：发当期军饷，结算欠饷并给担保，把终身半薪折成一笔等值补偿，结算口粮和被服的亏欠。1783年1月25日，国会只答应先发一个月饷、尽快结算账目，半薪折算退回再议。在场的军官肖写道，这份答复“远不能令人满意”，只是和平已近，部队才暂时安静。
after.en: The previous December the Continental Army had sent delegates to Congress with an address and petition. A congressional committee later summed it up in five articles: present pay; settlement of arrears with security for what was owed; commuting the promised half pay for life into a lump sum; and settling what was owed for rations and clothing. On 25 January 1783 Congress resolved only that the army would get one month's pay and that accounts would be settled as soon as possible; the half-pay commutation was sent back to committee. Major Samuel Shaw, an officer in the camp, wrote that this was "far from being satisfactory", but the certainty of peace kept the army quiet.

after.zh: 就在这时，一封匿名信在营中传开，号召军官们集会。华盛顿以3月11日的命令把会期定在15日，结果又引出了第二封匿名信。
after.en: Then an anonymous address began to circulate, calling the officers to a meeting. Washington, by an order of 11 March, set the meeting for the 15th instead, which drew a second anonymous address.

reason: '国会此前的答复' now evidenced as the 25 January resolves (extended D-E1); 'far from satisfactory' attributed to Shaw; '出卖大家' (stronger than 'mark for suspicion') removed; author's framing of Washington's difficulty removed from a record paragraph.

before.zh: 1783年春，独立战争接近尾声，和平已在眼前。地点是纽约州纽堡的军营，人物是总司令华盛顿和一群服役多年的军官，对面是远在费城、欠着他们饷的大陆会议。留下记述的是在场军官肖（Samuel Shaw），本篇关于现场的细节主要出自他的一封信。
before.en: In the spring of 1783 the Revolutionary War was drawing to a close and peace was in sight. The place was the army camp at Newburgh, New York; the people were the Commander-in-chief, Washington, and a group of officers who had served for years, facing the Continental Congress in far-off Philadelphia, which owed them their pay. The account is left by an officer who was present, Samuel Shaw, and most of the scene described here comes from a letter of his.

after.zh: 地点是纽约州纽堡的大陆军营地，独立战争已近尾声。主角是总司令华盛顿和一群服役多年的军官；3月15日的会议由盖茨少将主持。现场细节主要来自肖1783年4月的一封信，收在1847年出版的《肖日志》里。
after.en: The place was the Continental Army's camp at Newburgh, New York, with the War of Independence nearly over. The people were the commander-in-chief, George Washington, and officers who had served for years; the meeting of 15 March was chaired by Major General Horatio Gates. The details of the scene come mainly from a letter Shaw wrote in April 1783, printed in his journals in 1847.

reason: Removed unsupported '远在费城'; Shaw's account dated by its own provenance (D-E13) instead of an unverified recipient.

before.zh: 据肖记述，华盛顿发布开会命令时本没打算亲自到场；匿名文字流传之广让他改变了主意，还事先写好了讲稿。他上台先致歉，说自己出现在这里，并非发布那道命令时的本意。
before.en: According to Shaw, when Washington published the order to assemble he had no intention of appearing there himself. The wide circulation of the anonymous writings changed his mind, and he prepared his remarks in advance. He opened the meeting by apologizing, saying that his appearance there was by no means his intention when he published the order which directed them to assemble.

before.zh: 讲话开头就点了题："通过一份匿名的召集，有人试图把你们聚到一起。"接着他批评匿名信作者不够厚道——谁主张克制、主张再忍一忍，谁不按他的想法行事，就被标为可疑。这不是在替欠饷辩护，而是在拆开两件事：诉求可以谈，方式不能这样。
before.en: His address named the problem from the start: "By an anonymous summons, an attempt has been made to convene you together." He then faulted the anonymous author for a lack of charity — the man who should recommend moderation and longer forbearance, who should not think as he thinks and act as he advises, was marked for suspicion. This was not a defense of the unpaid wages; it separated two things: the demand could be talked about, but the method could not go on like this.

before.zh: 他请军官们不要采取任何"在冷静的理性之光下审视，会贬低你们至今保持的尊严、玷污你们至今保持的荣耀"的举动，把结算账目的事留给国会。
before.en: He asked the officers, on their part, not to take any measures which, "viewed in the calm hght of reason, will lessen the dignity, and sully the glory you have hitherto maintained," and to leave the settling of accounts to Congress.

before.zh: 然后是全场最被记住的一幕：他念一位国会议员的来信，读完第一段停了一下，取出眼镜，请大家包容他戴上，同时说到自己在他们的服役中头发已经白了，如今眼睛也快看不见了。肖说，这一下如此自然、毫无做作，胜过最精心设计的演说，直抵人心，可以看到人人眼含泪光。需要说明的是，这是肖一封信里的转述，不是逐字记录。
before.en: Then came the moment everyone remembers. He read a letter from a member of Congress, and after the first paragraph he made a short pause, took out his spectacles, and begged the indulgence of his audience while he put them on, observing at the same time that he had grown gray in their service, and now found himself growing blind. Shaw says the appeal was so natural, so unaffected, that it was superior to the most studied oratory; it forced its way to the heart, and you might see sensibility moisten every eye. Worth noting: this is Shaw's report in a letter, not a word-for-word record.

before.zh: 会议随即一致通过决议：军官们"以憎恶看待、以轻蔑拒绝"匿名信中的那些提议，并愤慨拒绝这种有损纪律与秩序的秘密召集。会议由盖茨少将主持，随后散会。一周后，3月22日国会决议：仍在役并服役至战争结束的军官，可得五年全薪，付现金或年息六厘的证券，以此代替原先承诺的终身半薪。
before.en: The meeting then passed a resolution unanimously: the officers viewed "with abhorrence" and rejected "with disdain" the propositions in the anonymous address, and resented with indignation the secret gathering that undermined all discipline and good order. Major General Horatio Gates presided, and the meeting was then dissolved. A week later, on 22 March, Congress resolved that officers now in service who continued to the end of the war should receive five years' full pay, in money or in securities bearing six per cent interest, in place of the half pay promised for life.

after.zh: 肖记下了华盛顿的开场：他先为自己到场致歉，说发布开会命令时本无此意；可匿名文字传得太广，他觉得必须向军队说明自己对这些文字的看法，于是借这个机会，并为了说得更清楚，事先把想法写了下来，请大家允许他照稿宣读。
after.en: Shaw recorded how Washington began. He apologised for appearing at all: that had been no part of his intention when he issued the order. But the anonymous papers had been circulated so busily that he felt he had to give the army his view of them, and to do it clearly he had "committed his thoughts to writing", which he asked leave to read.

after.zh: 讲稿第一句就点题：“有人用一份匿名的召集，试图把你们聚到一起。”他说，匿名信的作者文笔值得称道，可惜心术不正：谁主张克制、主张再忍耐一些，谁不按他的想法行事，就被他标为可疑。
after.en: The address opened bluntly: "By an anonymous summons, an attempt has been made to convene you together." The author of the anonymous address, he said, deserved credit for the goodness of his pen, but should have had the charity not "to mark for suspicion the man who should recommend moderation and longer forbearance".

after.zh: 他请军官们不要采取任何冷静下来看会“降低你们的尊严、玷污你们一向保持的荣誉”的举动，要相信国家许下的信义，相信国会会在军队解散之前把账目公平结清。
after.en: He asked the officers not to take any step which, viewed calmly, "will lessen the dignity, and sully the glory you have hitherto maintained", and to rely on "the plighted faith of your country" and on Congress to settle their accounts fairly before the army was disbanded.

after.zh: 讲完后，他说要念一位国会议员的来信，作为国会善待军队的佐证。读完第一段，他停了一下，取出眼镜，请大家包涵他戴上，并说自己为他们效力，头发已经白了，如今眼睛也快看不见了。肖写道，这一下如此自然、毫不做作，胜过最用心的演说，在场的人眼眶都湿了。要注意：这是肖的间接转述，不是逐字原话。
after.en: After the address he said he would read a letter from "a worthy member of that body", a congressman who had always been the army's friend, as evidence of Congress's goodwill. After the first paragraph he paused, took out his spectacles and asked their indulgence while he put them on, "observing at the same time, that he had grown gray in their service, and now found himself growing blind". Shaw thought it "superior to the most studied oratory". Note that this is Shaw's report of what Washington said, not his exact words.

after.zh: 华盛顿随即离场。会议在盖茨主持下一致通过决议：军官们“以憎恶看待、以轻蔑拒绝”那封匿名信中可耻的提议，并愤慨谴责有人暗中召集军官、完全破坏纪律与秩序的企图。一周后的3月22日，国会决议：在役并服役到战争结束的军官，可领五年全薪，付现金或年息六厘的证券，代替原先承诺的终身半薪。
after.en: Washington then left. With Gates presiding, the meeting resolved unanimously that the officers "view with abhorrence, and reject with disdain, the infamous propositions contained in a late anonymous address", and condemned the secret attempt to assemble them as subversive of all discipline. A week later, on 22 March, Congress resolved that officers serving to the end of the war would receive five years' full pay, in money or in securities at six per cent interest, instead of the half pay for life they had been promised.

reason: Speech-writing and congressman's letter now evidenced (extended D-E3, D-E4); 'trust Congress to settle accounts' evidenced (extended D-E8); interpretive sentence moved out of record paragraphs; resolution wording follows D-E9.

before.zh: 一种解释是：华盛顿把"要什么"和"怎么要"分开了。他没有说军官不该要钱——请愿里的五项他没有反驳；他反对的是匿名信把不同意见者打成可疑分子。会议决议的措辞跟着这个区分走：针对的是匿名信里的"提议"和秘密召集的方式，而不是请愿本身。
before.en: One explanation is that Washington separated "what is asked for" from "how it is asked for." He did not say the officers had no right to the money — he did not dispute the five items of the petition. What he opposed was the anonymous letter branding anyone who disagreed as a suspect. The wording of the meeting's resolution follows that distinction: it targets the "propositions" in the anonymous address and the manner of the secret gathering, not the petition itself.

before.zh: 另一种读法是把眼镜一幕看作一次有效的自我披露：一个身体上的真实变化被放进讲稿的节奏里（肖说他事先写好了讲稿），它不反驳任何人，只是把"我在和你们一起变老"变成在场可见的事实。它之所以动人，按肖的判断，正在于"自然"而不"做作"；但这也是肖的转述，我们无法核对原话与分寸。至于3月22日的国会决议与这场会议的关系，本篇只能说时间上紧随其后，因果不好断定。
before.en: Another reading treats the glasses moment as an effective piece of self-disclosure: a real physical change is placed into the rhythm of the prepared text (Shaw says he had written the speech out beforehand). It refutes no one; it simply turns "I am growing old along with you" into a fact visible to everyone present. It moved people, in Shaw's judgment, precisely because it was natural and not affected — but this too is Shaw's report, and we cannot check the original words or their measure. As for the link between Congress's resolution of 22 March and this meeting, this article can only say the one followed closely on the other; cause and effect cannot be established.

after.zh: 一种解释是（作者推断）：华盛顿把“要什么”和“怎么要”分开了。他没有说军官们的不满没有道理，而是请他们相信国会会结账；他反对的是匿名召集，以及把主张克制的人标为可疑。他本不打算到场，最后决定亲自去、照稿讲——按肖的转述，原因是匿名文字传得太广。
after.en: One interpretation, the author's, is that Washington separated what the officers wanted from how they were going about it. He did not say their grievance was baseless; he asked them to trust Congress to settle accounts. What he opposed was the anonymous summons and the branding of moderates as suspect. He had not meant to attend; by Shaw's account, he decided to come and read a prepared text because the anonymous papers had spread so widely.

after.zh: 眼镜一幕为什么有效，肖的说法是“自然、不做作”。但我们只有肖的转述，核对不了华盛顿的原话和语气。3月22日的国会决议紧跟在这次会议之后，两者有没有因果关系，现有材料说不清。
after.en: Why the spectacles moment worked, Shaw put down to its being natural and unaffected. But we have only his report and cannot check Washington's words or tone. The congressional resolution of 22 March followed hard on the meeting; whether one caused the other, the material we have cannot say.

reason: Removed '五项他没有反驳' (speech text does not support it) and the misattributed 'Shaw said he had written the speech'.

before.zh: 比如一个项目组的季度奖金拖了两个季度，有人在群里匿名号召大家周一一起去总部对质，并说"谁不去谁就是站在管理层那边"。负责人开全员会时，可以先把"钱确实欠着、我也没拿到"说清楚，再单独指出匿名串联把不愿出头的人架在火上——对准方式，不对准诉求，也别把要钱的人笼统叫成"闹事"。
before.en: Take a project team whose quarterly bonus has been delayed for two quarters. Someone posts anonymously in the group chat calling on everyone to go to headquarters together on Monday to confront management, adding that "if you don't go, you're on management's side." When the team lead holds an all-hands meeting, they can first state plainly that the money is indeed owed and that they have not been paid either, and then separately point out that anonymous organizing puts the people who don't want to stand out on the spot — aim at the method, not at the demand, and don't lump everyone asking for money together as troublemakers.

before.zh: 再比如，一个社区团队的报销积压半年，私下流传"负责人不作为"。负责人可以在会上讲一件属实的自身处境，比如自己也垫付了几个月、为此推掉了别的活，不求同情，只求让大家看见成本是共同的；然后给出一个具体的时间点和比对质更省力的出口，比如下周三前把单据汇总由他统一去催。前提是这件事属实，且后面真有动作，否则就成了表演。
before.en: Or take a community team whose reimbursements have piled up for half a year, with private talk that "the lead isn't doing anything." The lead can share one true fact about their own situation — say, that they have also fronted the costs for months and turned down other work because of it. Not to win sympathy, but so people can see the cost is shared. Then give a concrete deadline and an easier exit than confrontation, for example collecting all the receipts by next Wednesday so the lead can chase the payment in one go. The condition is that this must be true and that real action follows, otherwise it becomes theatre.

after.zh: 一个团队得知年终奖要延后发放。负责人可以等传言先到，也可以自己先开口：说清楚确定的部分（会发、大约延后多久、为什么），承认不确定的部分（具体日期还没定），并说明自己也在同一条船上。坏消息由负责人第一个说出来，比让大家从匿名渠道拼凑出来，少很多猜疑。
after.en: A team learns that its year-end bonus will be paid late. The manager can wait for the rumours to arrive first, or speak first: say what is certain (it will be paid, roughly how late, and why), admit what is not (the exact date is not fixed), and make clear that she is in the same position. Bad news delivered first by the person responsible breeds far less suspicion than news pieced together from anonymous channels.

after.zh: 再比如，一个社区团队的报销积压半年，私下流传"负责人不作为"。负责人可以在会上讲一件属实的自身处境，比如自己也垫付了几个月、为此推掉了别的活，不求同情，只求让大家看见成本是共同的；然后给出一个具体的时间点和比对质更省力的出口，比如下周三前把单据汇总由他统一去催。前提是这件事属实，且后面真有动作，否则就成了表演。
after.en: Or take a community team whose reimbursements have piled up for half a year, with private talk that "the lead isn't doing anything." The lead can share one true fact about their own situation — say, that they have also fronted the costs for months and turned down other work because of it. Not to win sympathy, but so people can see the cost is shared. Then give a concrete deadline and an easier exit than confrontation, for example collecting all the receipts by next Wednesday so the lead can chase the payment in one go. The condition is that this must be true and that real action follows, otherwise it becomes theatre.

reason: First scene duplicated the reflection's anonymous-post scenario; replaced with a 'deliver bad news yourself' scene. Second scene kept.

before.zh: 眼镜那一幕只有肖的一封信为据，且是转述；流传很广的那些"原话"并不在本篇材料里，所以别照着排戏，也别把它当成万能的情绪开关。匿名信的作者是谁有争议，本篇不讨论；五年全薪的证券后来是否兑现、折算是否合算，本篇未取材料，不下结论。同样别因此说"华盛顿一人挽救了共和国"——决议是与会军官一致通过的，主持会议的是盖茨少将，国会的决议在一周之后。
before.en: The glasses scene rests on a single letter from Shaw, and it is a retelling; the widely circulated "quotations" are not in the materials used here, so don't stage the scene from them, and don't treat it as an all-purpose emotional switch. Who wrote the anonymous address is disputed, and this article does not discuss it. Whether the securities for the five years' full pay were later honoured, and whether the commutation was a good deal, are questions this article has no materials on, so it draws no conclusion. In the same spirit, don't conclude that "Washington single-handedly saved the republic": the resolution was passed unanimously by the officers present, the meeting was chaired by Major General Gates, and Congress's resolution came a week later.

after.zh: 眼镜一幕只有肖的转述为据，流传很广的那句“原话”不在本篇材料里，别照着演，也别把它当成万能的情绪开关。匿名信出自何人，本篇材料只说是“不明身份的人”，这里不作讨论。五年全薪的证券后来兑现得怎样，本篇没有取材，不下结论。也别说“华盛顿一人挽救了共和国”：决议是与会军官一致通过的，会议由盖茨主持，国会的决议在一周之后。
after.en: The spectacles scene rests on Shaw's report alone, and the widely quoted line attributed to Washington is not in the material used here; do not stage it, and do not treat it as an emotional switch that always works. On who wrote the anonymous letters, the sources used here speak only of unknown persons, so this article does not go into it. How the five-year pay securities were later honoured is outside the material used here. Nor should anyone say that Washington alone saved the republic: the resolution was passed unanimously by the officers, Gates chaired the meeting, and Congress acted a week later.

reason: '作者有争议' replaced with what the evidence says (unknown persons).

before: 欠饷在前，匿名信在后：华盛顿在纽堡军官会上站哪一边
after: 欠饷是真的，匿名信也是真的：华盛顿在纽堡站在哪里

before: Back Pay First, Anonymous Letters Second: Where Washington Stood at the Newburgh Officers' Meeting
after: The Grievance Was Real, and So Was the Anonymous Letter: Washington at Newburgh

before: 1783年3月，纽约纽堡。军队的委屈有凭有据，但传达委屈的方式正在把不赞同的人打成可疑分子。一场临时改期的军官会议，成了如何传达坏消息的样本。
after: 1783年3月，独立战争快打完了，军官们的饷还欠着。有人用匿名信号召他们集会施压。华盛顿本不打算到场，最后还是去了。

before: March 1783, Newburgh, New York. The army's grievances were real and documented, but the way they were being voiced turned anyone who disagreed into a suspect. A hastily rescheduled officers' meeting became a case study in how to deliver bad news.
after: March 1783: the war was nearly over and the officers were still unpaid. Anonymous letters called them together to press their case. Washington had not meant to attend; in the end he went.

before: The scene details (Washington not intending to attend, having written his remarks in advance, the glasses moment, the audience's reaction) all come from a 1783 letter from Samuel Shaw to Rev. Eliot; this is a single source and a later retelling. The widely circulated direct quotations from the glasses moment are not in the materials used here, so the episode is stated only as Shaw reports it. The attribution of the anonymous address is disputed, and this article does not discuss it. What Washington thought is written only as Shaw reports him saying it; there is no speculation. The sequence between Congress's resolution of 22 March (five years' full pay) and the meeting of 15 March is on the record; no material supports a causal link. Whether the five years' full pay in securities was actually honoured is not covered by the materials used here, and no conclusion is drawn. The five articles of the army's petition and the wording of the resolution are quoted from the Journals of the Continental Congress, vol. 24 (1922 edition, with OCR errors); the wording is given as far as it can be read.
after: The details of the scene (that Washington had not meant to attend, that he read from a prepared text, the spectacles, the officers' reaction) come from a single letter Shaw wrote in April 1783, printed in his journals in 1847; it is one source, written after the event, and the passage used here does not name the recipient. The speech is taken from the printing in volume 24 of the Journals of the Continental Congress (OCR, with errors) and checked against the Wikisource text; the officers' resolution and the congressional resolution of 22 March come from the same volume. The five articles of the petition come from a later congressional committee report. "The previous December" is taken from context to mean December 1782. The authors of the anonymous letters are not identified in these sources, and the later fate of the pay securities was not researched.
